acks.detail: fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:2225-2242 — the parked `status.json.error` cell that appends the failing block of `<run dir>/acceptance.log` (M6), plus its exam fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_parked_error.mjs — Both arms run the real boot script, but only under _sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs's stubbed `git`/`gh`/`systemctl`/`claude` with `acceptance.log` seeded by the test itself. The end-to-end path the Claim's last clause names — the real gate wrapping the suite with `acceptanceWrap` (fleet/run-main.mjs:243-246), teeing to that path, and the resulting cell being published on a live sandbox VM's status page — needs a sandbox VM and GitHub, neither of which exists in this environment. The two sides do agree on the literal path here: run-main writes `<runDir>/acceptance.log` and boot reads `$(run_dir_path)/acceptance.log`, and boot's POSIX-awk `failing_block`/`has_failing_block` patterns match fleet/failing-block.mjs's START/END literal for literal. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

1 — plan-defect: the parked cell quotes the WHOLE acceptance.log when the log exists but carries no failure line. M6 conditions the ` — <block>` continuation on the log "carries a failure line"; the diff only tests `[ -f "$acceptance_log" ]` and then `[ -n "$failing" ]` (fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:2218-2222). But `failing_block`'s awk falls back to the entire file when it matches no start marker (fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:1364, `if (!start) { start = 1; stop = NR }` — the same fallback fleet/failing-block.mjs:36-38,63 documents: "A text with no start line ... is returned WHOLE"), so `$failing` is non-empty for ANY non-empty log. A run that parks with nothing ahead of base on a GREEN acceptance run — every task failed or BLOCKED on a green BASE, which the gate still tees to `<run dir>/acceptance.log` (fleet/run-main.mjs:243,246) — now writes the entire pytest session log into `status.json.error`. That is reachable, is a regression this diff introduces, and the fix is inside FILES. The task's Context prescribed exactly this shape ("when that file exists and the block is non-empty"), which is why it is prefixed plan-defect; M6 itself is unambiguous. The exam is complicit: fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_parked_error.mjs has only the seeded-failure arm and the file-absent arm, so the "carries a failure line" clause of M6 is unverified — a third arm with a green log is what settles it.
